Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verify" return nothing, and the two provisions that could plausibly host such a right — Section 5 (Fees and Payment, a pure revenue-share with payment flowing from Kubient to AP) and Section 6 (Use of Service, which imposes use restrictions but no verification or system-access mechanic) — grant Kubient no examination right. Section 1 requires AP to give "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation" only for the purpose of Kubient delivering the Services, not for compliance checking, and there is no remote or direct access to AP systems anywhere (no walk-away trigger). The absence of any audit right binding us is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost), so there is nothing to constrain and no redline is warranted — inserting audit limits would only create a vendor right that does not currently exist. Noted for the record but not flagged: since Impressions are "as measured by Kubient" and revenue flows to us, AP may separately wish to negotiate its own audit right over Kubient's records; that is a customer-favourable addition outside the scope of this rule.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: The only grant clause (para 2) runs to "Customer" alone and is expressly "revocable", with no reference to Affiliates or to contractors acting on our behalf, and no right of sublicense; para 8(a) (p0025) reinforces this by barring any third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

**What I found.** The sole grant clause (para 2, p0002) licenses the Auction Platform to "Customer" alone on a "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, **revocable**" basis. Para 8(a) (p0025) compounds this by prohibiting any third-party access to the Service without Kubient's prior written approval, so there is no notice-based path to bring AP affiliates or contractors under the licence.

**Why it fails the fallback.** The fallback requires at minimum that affiliates be covered on written notice and that the licence transfer to an M&A successor. The assignment clause (p0072) does permit assignment to an affiliate or a merger/stock-sale successor without consent, which satisfies the transferability limb. But affiliates and contractors remain excluded from the grant with only a Kubient-consent gate, and the licence is revocable at Kubient's discretion independent of the para 4 termination machinery — that is squarely the walk-away formulation.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** A single edit to p0002:
- adds "its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf" to the grantees;
- deletes "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable";
- ties revocation to expiration or termination under para 4 and confirms transfer to a successor under the existing assignment provisions.

I flagged this at the preferred position rather than the fallback because the at-will revocability is the more serious defect and cannot be fixed by an affiliate-notice mechanic alone. The comment offers affiliate-coverage-on-written-notice as a fallback if Kubient resists.

One drafting note I did **not** flag, since it is outside this rule: para 4(c)(ii) (p0021) refers to "the license granted under section 3," but the grant is in section 2 — worth correcting for consistency, particularly if the revocability edit above is accepted.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The only grant clause (para 2) runs to "Customer" alone and is expressly "revocable", with no reference to Affiliates or to contractors acting on our behalf, and no right of sublicense; para 8(a) (p0025) reinforces this by barring any third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval. That combination — a licence revocable at Kubient's discretion (independent of the termination machinery in para 4) with affiliates and contractors excluded and only a Kubient-consent path to add them — fails the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice) and sits in walk-away territory. The assignment clause (p0072) does permit assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or an M&A successor, which satisfies the transferability limb of the fallback, but that does not cure the affiliate/contractor exclusion or the at-will revocation right. Redline extends the grant to our Affiliates and contractors, ties revocation to expiry/termination under para 4, and confirms successor transfer.

In the event Customer shall utilize Kubient's ad serving technology as part of the Services, Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand (" "). Customer will ensure that its stories, articles, polls, videos, pictures, photographs, images, broadcasts, and any other type of content (collectively the "Content"), and each of its websites, devices, applications, podcasts, ads, emails, databases or any other types of mediums for which the Service is engaged (collectively the "Properties") contains or is linked to a privacy policy in accordance with applicable Law. Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.
p0072: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction. For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages payable by Customer)

- No liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated damages, shortfall charges or early-termination/minimum fees payable by AP appear anywhere in the Agreement — the preferred position is satisfied, so no redline was proposed.
- Section 5 is a revenue-share model in which money flows from Kubient to AP (within 7 days of Kubient's receipt); AP's only affirmative payment obligation is applicable sales/use taxes.
- The Section 4(a) carve-out entitling Kubient to "all fees generated during the termination period" is a revenue-share preservation on revenue actually generated during the 90-day notice window, not a Customer-payable termination fee, so it is not flagged.
- Section 7(a) mutually excludes punitive and special damages, reinforcing the absence of penalty exposure.
- Caveat recorded in the rationale: fee mechanics live in the Exhibits, which are outside this document and should be reviewed for any minimum-revenue or shortfall commitment payable by AP.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated damages, shortfall charges or early-termination fees payable by AP appear anywhere in the Agreement, so the rule's preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) is met. Section 5 is a revenue-share arrangement under which payments flow from Kubient to AP, and AP's only monetary obligations are applicable sales/use taxes. The Section 4(a) statement that Kubient "shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" is not a Customer-payable termination fee — it merely preserves Kubient's revenue-share on revenue actually generated during the 90-day notice period, and the mutual limitation of liability in Section 7(a) excludes punitive and special damages. Note for completeness that fee mechanics sit in the Exhibits, which are not part of this document and should be checked for any minimum-revenue or shortfall commitment payable by AP.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 14. General Provisions.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and a read of all 75 paragraphs (including the General Provisions in Section 14(a)–(i)) confirms the Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind — no CGL, no professional/tech E&O, no cyber, no workers' compensation, and no certificate requirement. This is a services/hosting arrangement where Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per Section 9(b)(iii), collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information (data), and per Section 3(g) receives Requests (data sent from Customer). A vendor that processes such data with zero required coverage falls into the rule's walk-away territory rather than the fallback (which still requires E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M), so the omission is material notwithstanding the rule's low severity. Kubient's broad indemnity in Section 10(a) is unbacked by any solvency assurance, which is precisely the gap insurance addresses. Remedy: insert a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Kubient handles Customer/visitor data, workers' compensation as required by Law, and certificates on request, maintained through the Term and one year thereafter. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is available in negotiation if Kubient's existing program is more modest.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as Kubient collects and stores visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii) and the Agreement currently requires no coverage at all. Our position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can discuss lower cyber and E&O limits if Kubient's current program is more modest.

ops.text: Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient collects, processes or stores Customer data or visitor data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Kubient shall also maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: 14. General Provisions.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and a read of all 75 paragraphs (including the General Provisions in Section 14(a)–(i)) confirms the Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind — no CGL, no professional/tech E&O, no cyber, no workers' compensation, and no certificate requirement. This is a services/hosting arrangement where Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per Section 9(b)(iii), collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information (data), and per Section 3(g) receives Requests (data sent from Customer). A vendor that processes such data with zero required coverage falls into the rule's walk-away territory rather than the fallback (which still requires E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M), so the omission is material notwithstanding the rule's low severity. Kubient's broad indemnity in Section 10(a) is unbacked by any solvency assurance, which is precisely the gap insurance addresses. Remedy: insert a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Kubient handles Customer/visitor data, workers' compensation as required by Law, and certificates on request, maintained through the Term and one year thereafter. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is available in negotiation if Kubient's existing program is more modest.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, WARRANTY).**

**What the document has (compliant elements):**
- **Duration/scope exceed preferred** — Kubient's warranties in ¶9(b) run for the whole Term with no 12-month or 90-day sunset: performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from errors materially affecting utility (p0038), no viruses/malicious code (p0036), compliance with Laws (p0041), plus IP non-infringement and ownership.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** — ¶13 opens with "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language is properly carved back. No walk-away risk.

**Why it still fails the fallback:**
- **No warranty remedy anywhere.** "Refund" appears nowhere in the agreement, and there is no re-performance, repair or replacement right. The only recourse is the general 30-day cure/termination right in ¶4(b), which is not a warranty remedy. Remedy is a material term of both the preferred and the fallback position ("same remedies"), so this is a genuine fallback failure rather than a minor sub-element.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** a single inserted sentence after p0041 giving us, at Kubient's option, re-performance, repair/replacement or a refund of fees paid or payable for the non-conforming Service or deliverable, expressly without limiting our other rights and remedies. I left the warranty period and the disclaimer untouched since both already sit at or above the preferred position — the smallest edit that reaches compliance.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Kubient gives affirmative warranties that run for the whole Term (no 12-month/90-day cut-off), including performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from errors materially affecting utility (p0038), no malicious code (p0036) and compliance with Laws (p0041), and the paragraph 13 disclaimer expressly carves out "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement", so it does not swallow the express warranty. Duration and scope therefore exceed the preferred position. However, the Agreement contains no warranty remedy at all — there is no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund right anywhere (only the general 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b)), and "refund" appears nowhere in the document. Remedy is a material term of both the preferred and fallback positions, so we added the standard remedy sentence at Kubient's option after paragraph 9(b), preserving our other rights. We did not touch the period or disclaimer, which are already compliant; the absence of express "professional and workmanlike" wording is covered by the industry-standards warranty and is not flagged.

Original paragraphs:
p0034: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
p0038: (vi) any services provided by it shall comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility;
p0062: 13. Disclaimer. Except as expressly set forth herein, the Services are provided on an "as is," "where is," and "as available" basis, and, to the maximum extent permitted by Law, Kubient disclaims, and Customer hereby waives, all representations and warranties, express or implied, arising by operation of Law or otherwise, except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement, including but not limited to the implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, as well as any warranties arising from a course of dealing, usage or trade practice. Kubient makes no representation or warranty and expressly disclaims, and Customer understands and acknowledges, that there is no guarantee that any minimum level of revenue or profit will be generated by either Party as a result of the Services or this Agreement.

**Finding: MISSING** (INSURANCE — Vendor insurance)

**What I checked**
- Searched the full text for "insurance" — zero hits.
- Read all 75 paragraphs, including the full General Provisions block (§14(a)–(i)) and the definitions, in case coverage was buried in an unlabeled subsection or exhibit reference.

**Why it's a finding, not a nit**
The Agreement imposes no insurance obligation at all — no CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp, or certificate delivery. That matters here because Kubient is squarely a data-touching vendor:
- §9(b)(iii): Kubient "collect[s], maintain[s], manage[s] and stor[es]" visitor information (data);
- §3(g): "Request(s)" are data sent from Customer to Kubient;
- §2: Kubient hosts the Auction Platform.

A vendor processing this kind of data with zero required coverage is the rule's **walk-away** scenario, not the fallback (which still demands E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). It also compounds a real exposure: Kubient gives a broad indemnity in §10(a) covering the Services, the Auction Platform, Creative, and warranty breaches — with no coverage behind it, that indemnity is only as good as Kubient's balance sheet. Insurance is exactly the mechanic that backstops it.

**Remedy** (validated, `ok:true`)
Inserted a new §14(j) at the **preferred** position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; E&O USD 2M; cyber USD 5M where Kubient handles Customer or visitor data; workers' comp as required by Law; certificates on request; maintained through the Term plus one year. Drafted with Kubient as the bound party — this is a one-way covenant running in our favor, consistent with the seed precedent.

Two notes for the negotiation:
- I tied the cyber trigger to "Customer data or visitor data" rather than a defined "Customer Data" term, because the Agreement has no such definition — the operative data concepts are the §9(b)(iii) visitor data and §3(g) Requests. Worth confirming that phrasing survives any later definitional cleanup.
- The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is flagged in the comment as available if Kubient's existing program is more modest. Given this is a revenue-share ad-tech deal rather than a large-spend engagement, expect pushback on the USD 5M cyber limit; that is the line I'd concede first, and I'd hold hardest on cyber existing at all plus certificates on request.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no hits, and a read of all 75 paragraphs (including the General Provisions in Section 14(a)–(i)) confirms the Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind — no CGL, no professional/tech E&O, no cyber, no workers' compensation, and no certificate requirement. This is a services/hosting arrangement where Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per Section 9(b)(iii), collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information (data), and per Section 3(g) receives Requests (data sent from Customer). A vendor that processes such data with zero required coverage falls into the rule's walk-away territory rather than the fallback (which still requires E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M), so the omission is material notwithstanding the rule's low severity. Kubient's broad indemnity in Section 10(a) is unbacked by any solvency assurance, which is precisely the gap insurance addresses. Remedy: insert a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Kubient handles Customer/visitor data, workers' compensation as required by Law, and certificates on request, maintained through the Term and one year thereafter. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is available in negotiation if Kubient's existing program is more modest.

Original paragraphs:
p0063: 14. General Provisions.
p0073: (i) This Agreement is intended for the sole and exclusive benefit of the Parties hereto, is not intended to confer any rights or benefits on any third party, and only the Parties may enforce such Agreement. This Agreement shall be binding on both Parties when signed on behalf of each Party, and may be signed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original and both of which when taken together will constitute one and the same agreement. Fax or electronically scanned copies of such executed documents may be used in lieu of the originals for any purpose.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of February, 2020 (the "Effective Date"), is by and between Kubient Inc., with offices located at 330 7th Avenue, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10001 ("Kubient") and The Associated Press, a New York not-for-profit corporation with principal place of business located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10281 (the "Customer"). Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". WHEREAS, Customer wishes to increase the revenue derived from its traffic, content, websites, applications, podcasts, audience and database, and would like to retain Kubient to support and assist in that process as described herein; For good and valuable consideration, the receipt of which is acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

Rendered redline:
p0073: (i) This Agreement is intended for the sole and exclusive benefit of the Parties hereto, is not intended to confer any rights or benefits on any third party, and only the Parties may enforce such Agreement. This Agreement shall be binding on both Parties when signed on behalf of each Party, and may be signed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed to be an original and both of which when taken together will constitute one and the same agreement. Fax or electronically scanned copies of such executed documents may be used in lieu of the originals for any purpose.
Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient collects, processes or stores Customer data or visitor data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Kubient shall also maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as Kubient collects and stores visitor data under Section 9(b)(iii) and the Agreement currently requires no coverage at all. Our position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber liability of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can discuss lower cyber and E&O limits if Kubient's current program is more modest.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Kubient agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment or volume restriction on AP:

- **§1 (Services)** — Services are engaged per-Exhibit on a specific-engagement basis, and the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive, with AP free to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties.
- **§5 (Fees and Payment)** — Pure revenue-share on revenue actually generated; AP pays no subscription or committed fee, and there is no shortfall, true-up or take-or-pay mechanic.
- Term searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "volume" and "purchase" surfaced only unrelated text: the Winning Bid Price floor that AP itself sets (p0014), the §13 disclaimer that no minimum revenue is guaranteed (p0062), and the material-breach "commits" reference (p0016).

This sits at the **preferred position** (no minimum commitment; fees for usage/ordered services only). Noted in the rationale but not flagged: §4(a) prevents convenience termination during the one-year Initial Term — but with no committed spend, that lock-in creates no take-or-pay exposure under this rule (and term/termination flexibility is properly addressed under the termination rule, not double-flagged here).

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, spend, impression or volume commitment on AP. Services are engaged on a per-Exhibit basis (§1), and §5 (Fees and Payment) is a pure revenue-share on revenue actually generated, with no shortfall, take-or-pay or minimum-guarantee mechanic anywhere (searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "volume", "purchase" return only unrelated references — the Winning Bid Price floor AP itself sets (p0014) and the §13 disclaimer that no minimum revenue is guaranteed (p0062)). §1 also confirms the arrangement is non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from selling Inventory through others. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage/ordered services only), so no redline. Noted only for context: §4(a) locks the one-year Initial Term against convenience termination, but since there is no committed spend that lock-in creates no take-or-pay exposure under this rule.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: missing** (TRANSITION) — validated redline submitted.

**What I found.** The Agreement's only exit machinery is section 4(c) (p0019–p0022), which covers four things: Kubient ceases the Services, the section 3 license is revoked, Customer stops using the Services/Auction Platform, and each Party "will return **or destroy**" the other's Confidential Information. Nothing else in the document addresses exit — searches for data return, export, deletion and transition turned up only security obligations (section 8(iii), p0035) and the general survival language (p0070).

**Why that fails the fallback.** This is a hosted auction-platform deal in which Kubient collects, maintains and stores AP data and receives "Requests" from AP. Yet:
- there is no obligation to **return** AP's data at all — the Confidential Information clause is elective ("return *or* destroy"), and the election sits with the holder, i.e. Kubient;
- no format requirement, no export deadline, no deletion certification;
- no wind-down or transition assistance of any duration.

That is below the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days) and edges toward walk-away territory, since Kubient could lawfully destroy AP material on termination without ever handing it back.

**Redline.** A new (v)–(vi) inserted after p0022, inside the existing effects-of-termination list: six months' transition assistance on request at Kubient's then-current rates, return of Content, Requests and other Customer data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. I used the Agreement's own defined terms ("Content," "Requests") rather than importing an undefined "Customer Data," since that term does not appear in this document.

One drafting note worth flagging to the deal team: the fallback (90 days) is offered in the comment, so the negotiator has room to trade duration without reopening the data-return and certification mechanics, which are the parts that matter most here.

Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 4(c) is the only effects-of-termination provision and it addresses just cessation of Services, revocation of the license, Customer's cessation of use, and mutual return-or-destruction of Confidential Information (at the holder's election). There is no obligation for Kubient to return AP's data (Content, Requests or other data it collects, maintains or stores under section 8(iii)) in a usable format, no export deadline, no certified deletion, and no wind-down or transition assistance anywhere in the Agreement. In a hosted auction-platform arrangement this falls below even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition and data-return language into section 4(c).

Original paragraphs:
p0019: (c) Upon termination of the Agreement:
p0020: (i) Kubient will cease providing the Services;
p0021: (ii) the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked, (iii) Customer will promptly cease use of the Services and the Auction Platform;
p0022: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of February, 2020 (the "Effective Date"), is by and between Kubient Inc., with offices located at 330 7th Avenue, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10001 ("Kubient") and The Associated Press, a New York not-for-profit corporation with principal place of business located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10281 (the "Customer"). Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". WHEREAS, Customer wishes to increase the revenue derived from its traffic, content, websites, applications, podcasts, audience and database, and would like to retain Kubient to support and assist in that process as described herein; For good and valuable consideration, the receipt of which is acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:
Customer: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of February, 2020 (the "Effective Date"), is by and between Kubient Inc., with offices located at 330 7th Avenue, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10001 ("Kubient") and The Associated Press, a New York not-for-profit corporation with principal place of business located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10281 (the "Customer"). Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". WHEREAS, Customer wishes to increase the revenue derived from its traffic, content, websites, applications, podcasts, audience and database, and would like to retain Kubient to support and assist in that process as described herein; For good and valuable consideration, the receipt of which is acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

Rendered redline:
p0022: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.
(v) at Customer's request, Kubient will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following such termination or expiration at Kubient's then-current rates; and (vi) within thirty (30) days of such termination or expiration, Kubient will return to Customer, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all Content, Requests and other Customer data then in Kubient's possession or control, and will thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added an orderly exit: up to six months of transition assistance at Kubient's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. As drafted, section 4(c) lets Kubient simply stop the Services and destroy material with no obligation to hand our data back; we can accept a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

Document: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of Feb

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-f601506e","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 10(a) gives us a broad Vendor-side defence and indemnity covering third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative served through it, Kubient's breach of its representations and warranties (which include its ownership of all IP in the Service and Auction Platform (p0039–p0040) and its compliance with applicable Law (p0041)), and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Because it captures any third-party Claim \"arising out of or in connection with\" the Services and Platform, it covers IP infringement/misappropriation allegations, unlawful conduct and Kubient's misconduct, so it meets (indeed exceeds) the preferred position, with no super-cap needed. Section 11 supplies the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, and the liability cap in Section 9(a) expressly carves out indemnification liability. Minor note only, not a deviation: our own indemnity in Section 10(b) is mirrored rather than strictly limited to Customer Content/Properties and breach of law (it also reaches misuse of the Services/Platform and Customer's acts or omissions); that is customary reciprocal drafting and does not undercut the Vendor indemnity, so we do not redline it.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-4c56d202","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The Agreement contains no intellectual property or ownership provision. Section 6(a) allocates liability for the Content and Properties to Customer but does not confirm Customer's ownership; Section 9(c)(i) is only a warranty that Customer owns the Content; Section 14(b) covers names, trademarks and logos only. Nothing addresses ownership of the \"Requests\" data sent by Customer to Kubient, visitor/audience data collected via the Auction Platform, or any deliverables, reports or work product created for Customer, and there is no licence-back of Kubient IP embedded in deliverables. For AP, whose content and audience data are its core assets, silence leaves ownership of the data flowing to Kubient and of any Kubient-created work product unresolved. There is no assignment of Customer IP to Kubient (so no walk-away trigger), but the rule expects an ownership clause and no usable clause exists, so we have added one at the preferred position: AP retains all rights in Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient assigns deliverables while retaining its pre-existing platform and technology subject to a perpetual, royalty-free licence for embedded IP; no joint ownership.","proposal":"Add ownership clause: AP retains all rights in Content, Properties and data; Kubient assigns deliverables and licenses embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-df7f8e5e","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 7 (\"Limitation of Liability\") contains only a mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages (with indemnification and confidentiality carved out of that exclusion). There is no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement — a full-text search for \"exceed\" and \"aggregate liability\" returns no cap language — so both parties' direct liability is unlimited and the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs) is not met on a material term. The commercial structure is a revenue share in which Kubient pays Customer (Section 5), so a pure fees-based cap would be illusory; we therefore added the preferred formulation with a USD 1,000,000 floor, applied mutually, with indemnification, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped, and Section 5 revenue-share payments excluded from \"damages\". The existing consequential-damages waiver is already mutual and is left intact.","proposal":"Add a mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 7","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-6f7204ad","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The clause is mutual and gives AP the free-assignment carve-out the preferred position requires: AP may assign without Kubient's consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that \"shall not be unreasonably withheld.\" A full-text search returns no \"change of control\" language anywhere in the Agreement, and the termination provisions contain no Kubient right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control, so the walk-away triggers are absent. Two preferred sub-elements are missing but are not material enough to redline: there is no express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor, and the consent carve-out runs to both parties rather than being one-way in our favour (i.e., at least at the fallback \"mutual right to assign to successors\" position). The \"non-transferable, non-assignable\" wording in the § 2 Kubient License is a standard licence-scope limitation on the technology grant, not a restriction on assignment of the Agreement, which § (h) governs and which expressly binds and benefits \"successors and permitted assigns.\"","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-98ad9633","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"No exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation binds AP anywhere in the Agreement. To the contrary, the Kubient Services clause (p0001) expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms AP remains free to offer Inventory through other agents or sell it to third parties, so AP retains full freedom to use other ad platforms. The remaining \"exclusive\" references are unrelated and non-restrictive: p0002 grants AP a non-exclusive licence (in our favour), p0064 is an exclusive jurisdiction/venue provision, p0065 concerns each Party's own trademarks, and p0072/p0073 are entire-agreement and no-third-party-beneficiary boilerplate. Searches for sole-source, requirements-purchase, non-compete and competitor-restriction language returned nothing. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity obligation on Customer); no redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-f0e77df4","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"No liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated damages, shortfall charges or early-termination fees payable by AP appear anywhere in the Agreement, so the rule's preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) is met. Section 5 is a revenue-share arrangement under which payments flow from Kubient to AP, and AP's only monetary obligations are applicable sales/use taxes. The Section 4(a) statement that Kubient \"shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period\" is not a Customer-payable termination fee — it merely preserves Kubient's revenue-share on revenue actually generated during the 90-day notice period, and the mutual limitation of liability in Section 7(a) excludes punitive and special damages. Note for completeness that fee mechanics sit in the Exhibits, which are not part of this document and should be checked for any minimum-revenue or shortfall commitment payable by AP.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-41cc90bd","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The only grant clause (para 2) runs to \"Customer\" alone and is expressly \"revocable\", with no reference to Affiliates or to contractors acting on our behalf, and no right of sublicense; para 8(a) (p0025) reinforces this by barring any third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval. That combination — a licence revocable at Kubient's discretion (independent of the termination machinery in para 4) with affiliates and contractors excluded and only a Kubient-consent path to add them — fails the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice) and sits in walk-away territory. The assignment clause (p0072) does permit assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or an M&A successor, which satisfies the transferability limb of the fallback, but that does not cure the affiliate/contractor exclusion or the at-will revocation right. Redline extends the grant to our Affiliates and contractors, ties revocation to expiry/termination under para 4, and confirms successor transfer.","proposal":"Extend the Auction Platform licence to Customer's Affiliates and contractors, remove at-will revocability, and confirm transfer to a successor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-95b59958","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"No non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territory covenant binds AP anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for \"compet\", \"exclusiv\" and \"shall not\" surface only Kubient-side warranties, AP's own content/creative standards, forum-selection and IP-ownership language — none restricting AP's businesses, purchases or development. Section 1 affirmatively disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP may offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties, which matches the preferred position (no restriction on Customer). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-3c69dc5a","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Clause 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. The Initial Term is one (1) year — not a multi-year commitment — so the absence of a convenience right during that period does not trigger the \"missing behaviour\" deviation (which applies to terms longer than 12 months), and thereafter AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice, i.e. within the fallback's 60–90 day window. There is no early-termination fee or acceleration: under clause 5 AP pays no fees at all (revenue share flows from Kubient to AP), and Kubient's entitlement to \"all fees generated during the termination period\" is simply its continuing revenue share on impressions actually monetised during the notice period, not a penalty, so there are no prepaid fees to refund. On Kubient's side, its convenience right also requires ninety (90) days' notice and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so the walk-away trigger (vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice) is not met. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position and are noted rather than flagged: AP's notice period is 90 days rather than 30, and Kubient's convenience right is not expressly confined to the end of a renewal term. If the term is later extended beyond one year or renewal terms are lengthened, we should revisit and add a 30-day AP convenience right with a pro-rata refund mechanic.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-11c01e74","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right exercisable by Kubient against the Customer. Searches for \"audit\", \"inspect\", \"records\" and \"verify\" return nothing, and the two provisions that could plausibly host such a right — Section 5 (Fees and Payment, a pure revenue-share with payment flowing from Kubient to AP) and Section 6 (Use of Service, which imposes use restrictions but no verification or system-access mechanic) — grant Kubient no examination right. Section 1 requires AP to give \"reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation\" only for the purpose of Kubient delivering the Services, not for compliance checking, and there is no remote or direct access to AP systems anywhere (no walk-away trigger). The absence of any audit right binding us is better than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost), so there is nothing to constrain and no redline is warranted — inserting audit limits would only create a vendor right that does not currently exist. Noted for the record but not flagged: since Impressions are \"as measured by Kubient\" and revenue flows to us, AP may separately wish to negotiate its own audit right over Kubient's records; that is a customer-favourable addition outside the scope of this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-3d9a5903","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 14(a) applies Delaware substantive law — an accepted fallback jurisdiction — with exclusive venue in the state and federal courts in New York, New York, which matches our preferred forum. There is no foreign law, no foreign venue and no arbitration seated abroad; Section 8's AAA Commercial Arbitration clause is a domestic (US) forum, so it does not reach walk-away territory. Two minor points noted rather than flagged: the governing law is Delaware rather than our preferred New York, and Section 8's mandatory AAA arbitration sits awkwardly alongside the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a) — worth clarifying in negotiation, but not a failure of the fallback on the material terms of this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-6f5e2bd0","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Searches for \"most favored\", \"no less favorable\", \"favourable\", \"best rates\", \"favor\" and \"pricing\" return nothing, and a full read of the single section confirms the Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation, price-matching or \"terms no less favourable\" undertaking anywhere. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage/ordered services only), so no redline. Noted only for context: §4(a) locks the one-year Initial Term against convenience termination, but since there is no committed spend that lock-in creates no take-or-pay exposure under this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-aa678cbd","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"employ or engage\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"personnel\", \"non-compete\" and \"directly or indirectly\" return no restrictive covenant anywhere in the Agreement; the only employment-related general provision is the independent-contractor clause (p0066), and the sole references to hiring/employment sit in the indemnity and confidentiality provisions.
