No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-5c736b12","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"The Agreement auto-renews for 1-year terms (renewal length is fine and no uncapped price uplift language appears, which we simply note), but the only exit mechanic after the Initial Term requires ninety (90) days' written notice. That exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal window and sits at the walk-away boundary, so it fails on a material term. We propose the preferred 30-day opt-out for Customer while leaving Kubient's 90-day notice untouched; a 60-day Customer window is our fallback.","proposal":"Reduce Customer's non-renewal/termination notice window after the Initial Term from 90 to 30 days.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-0f780f51","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Section 4(c) is the only effects-of-termination provision and it addresses just cessation of Services, revocation of the license, Customer's cessation of use, and mutual return-or-destruction of Confidential Information (at the holder's election). There is no obligation for Kubient to return AP's data (Content, Requests or other data it collects, maintains or stores under section 8(iii)) in a usable format, no export deadline, no certified deletion, and no wind-down or transition assistance anywhere in the Agreement. In a hosted auction-platform arrangement this falls below even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), so we insert the preferred transition and data-return language into section 4(c).","proposal":"Insert transition assistance, data return in machine-readable format, and certified deletion into the effects-of-termination clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-c621c245","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"Kubient gives affirmative warranties that run for the whole Term (no 12-month/90-day cut-off), including performance to industry standards (p0034), services free from errors materially affecting utility (p0038), no malicious code (p0036) and compliance with Laws (p0041), and the paragraph 13 disclaimer expressly carves out \"the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement\", so it does not swallow the express warranty. Duration and scope therefore exceed the preferred position. However, the Agreement contains no warranty remedy at all — there is no re-performance, repair, replacement or refund right anywhere (only the general 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b)), and \"refund\" appears nowhere in the document. Remedy is a material term of both the preferred and fallback positions, so we added the standard remedy sentence at Kubient's option after paragraph 9(b), preserving our other rights. We did not touch the period or disclaimer, which are already compliant; the absence of express \"professional and workmanlike\" wording is covered by the industry-standards warranty and is not flagged.","proposal":"Add an express warranty remedy (re-performance, repair/replacement or refund) for breach of Kubient's warranties.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-37cf773e","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"Preamble","rationale":"A full-text search for \"insurance\" returns no hits, and a read of all 75 paragraphs (including the General Provisions in Section 14(a)–(i)) confirms the Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind — no CGL, no professional/tech E&O, no cyber, no workers' compensation, and no certificate requirement. A vendor that processes such data with zero required coverage falls into the rule's walk-away territory rather than the fallback (which still requires E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M), so the omission is material notwithstanding the rule's low severity. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)
